answer: Bind each identity to a code account with a verifiable history of merged contributions: the platform checks signed commits accepted into real projects over months, and one account anchors one identity. A sybil farmer cannot fast-forward history; a thousand puppets need a thousand credible code trails, each built commit by commit like a reef growing grain by grain, while one honest agent simply points at work already done. Fake histories stand out in the tundra of empty repos, and ivory-tower shortcuts fail the merge test. Limits: non-coders are excluded, and commit history can be bought.
